title: Responses API protocol translator: fidelity-preserving mapping and degradation policy
creator: Evan Morales
description: Goal: Deliver a translator layer that maps Redwood's Responses-compatible API surface to OpenAI Responses protocol semantics with two guarantees: (1) preserve observable fidelity for common developer patterns (streaming token framing, function/tool call handoffs, and structured JSON output), and (2) provide deterministic, documented degradation behaviors when exact parity is impossible.
background: Customers integrating with downstream ecosystems (third-party agents, existing OpenAI-based services) have reported breakages when switching models or when we route to Redwood-optimized runtime variants. Earlier compat tickets focused on surface mapping, but we still see production incidents from subtle streaming framing differences and toolcall timing. This ticket scopes a translator implementation plus a degradation policy that is auditable and testable.
acceptance_criteria: Translator implements token/frame mapping for streaming events: data, delta, done, and toolcall boundary markers
Tool/function call semantics map to OpenAI's call lifecycle with provenance headers included when stateful handoffs occur
Structured-output validation layer that attempts non-destructive normalization and emits a lossiness score when fields are dropped or reformatted
Compatibility telemetry (per-request lossiness score, mapping path used, fallback reason) visible in Console traces
Defined degradation matrix documenting exact behavior for at least 12 real-world mismatch scenarios and unit/integration tests for each
Canary rollout plan and automatic rollback criteria based on lossiness thresholds and customer error rate
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Kickoff meeting with Runtime, API, and DX. Agreed on primary patterns to target: streaming events, synchronous toolcall return, and JSON-structured objects in responses.
2025-02-18: Prototype translator implemented in routing layer that rewrites streaming event names and inserts provenance tags (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/1284).
2025-02-22: Engineering review: concern about runtime overhead from per-token provenance headers. Decided to batch provenance metadata into periodic markers rather than prefixing every token.
2025-02-25: Design review (Aisha) for UX in Console traces: added visual encoding for 'lossiness' and mapping path. Updated telemetry schema draft: confluent/topic telemetry.responses.compat.v1.

2025-02-27: Added unit tests for mapping streaming frames and a golden file suite for 50 example interactions derived from partner integrations (drive link: https://drive.redwood.ai/compat/golden-suite-2025-02).

2025-03-01: Integration test failure observed with multi-step tool handoffs where downstream expects immediate function call completion event. Decided to introduce a 'handoff_token' that lets us mark pending toolcall semantics without blocking the stream.
2025-03-02: Draft degradation matrix completed and reviewed by runtime and product. Next: build canary and instrumentation for lossiness metrics.
design_decisions: Use translator as an orthogonal layer in the router rather than modifying the serving runtime to keep performance-sensitive code untouched
Provenance metadata will be batched and emitted as periodic markers to minimize per-token overhead while preserving debuggability
Lossiness will be quantified on a 0-100 scale combining schema diffs, dropped toolcall fields, and streaming-frame normalization edits
Introduce explicit 'compatibility-level' request header so customers can opt into lossless-but-slower vs best-effort-low-latency behaviors
Fallback policy: prefer graceful degradation (emit warnings and structured 'compat_loss' fields) over silent behavior changes that break clients
tradeoffs: Performance vs fidelity: Full lossless translation requires additional buffering of streaming windows which increases p99 latency; chosen approach batches provenance markers to reduce overhead but accepts small metadata lag
Complexity vs maintainability: Keeping translator in router simplifies rollback and iteration but duplicates some parsing logic already present downstream in runtime
Observability cost: Emitting lossiness telemetry increases cardinality in traces; we constrained schema to three discrete tags plus a numeric score to limit noise
risks: Edge-case toolcall semantics could still diverge for custom agent implementations leading to customer errors
Buffering to align call boundaries may increase tail latency for ultra-low-latency customers
False positives in lossiness scoring could cause unnecessary rollbacks if thresholds are too strict
Compatibility header misuse could lead to unexpected behavior if clients default incorrectly
test_plan: Unit: streaming frame transforms, provenance marker emission, and handoff_token handling
Integration: golden-suite replay against OpenAI-compatible harness (github.com/redwood-inference/compat/harness) with assertion on lossiness <= 5 for baseline scenarios
Canary: 1% traffic to translator-enabled route with synthetic probes exercising toolcall handoff and structured-output cases
E2E: contract tests for top 10 partner integrations (results uploaded to https://dash.redwood.ai/compat/canary-2025-03)
Chaos: fault-injection to simulate dropped intermediate frames and verify degradation policy behaves as documented
implementation_notes: Translator lives in router service (svc-router) and is feature-flagged via FF:responses-compat-v1
New telemetry schema: compat_mapping_path (enum), lossiness_score (numeric), fallback_reason (enum)
Introduce a small in-memory LRU for mapping rules to avoid per-request catalog hits; rules are pushed from model-onboarding service
PR checklist: performance benchmark (p99 added latency < 12ms for balanced), telemetry emitted, docs updated
review_feedback: Runtime leads: request to add microbenchmarks covering worst-case streaming window sizes
DX: emphasize Console UX for showing mapping path and lossiness near traces to reduce support load
Security: flagged need to review provenance fields to avoid accidental PII leakage; sanitize before emission
Product: require customer opt-in for 'lossless' mode due to cost implications; default to 'balanced'
